boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus settings for studying, making, gathering, performing, and taking part in college life.

cards.title: Lowry Center
cards.subtitle: Campus dining and gathering space
cards.notes: Use the dining hall as a planned meet-up point between classes, then leave time to sit and catch up rather than treating it as a quick stop.
cards.short_summary: The College identifies Lowry as its central dining space, with room to gather between classes and at day’s end.
cards.evidence_claim: The College describes Lowry Center as the heart of campus dining, with space to gather between classes or at the end of the day.
cards.access_notes: Dining access and service availability may vary; check College dining information before going.

cards.title: The Alley
cards.subtitle: Lowry Center’s lower-level collaborative space
cards.notes: Bring a group task, game, or casual meeting and use the movable setup for your plan; reserve or confirm availability when an event is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: The Alley combines study rooms, gathering areas, and adaptable space in Lowry’s lower level.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wooster Voice reports that The Alley opened as a student-oriented, multipurpose collaborative space with group-study and club-meeting rooms.
cards.source_title: The Alley provides a multi-use space for students
cards.access_notes: Located on the basement floor of Lowry Center; programming and room availability can affect access.

cards.title: Collaborative Research Environment (CoRE)
cards.subtitle: Andrews Library
cards.notes: Start a shared research or media project here: brainstorm together, then move from library help to writing or digital-media support as needed.
cards.short_summary: CoRE is an Andrews Library setting designed for collaborative research, projects, and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says CoRE gives students technology and resources to research, brainstorm, and collaborate with faculty and other students.
cards.access_notes: CoRE is on the main floor of Andrews Library; consult library guidance for current access and support hours.

cards.title: Gault Library for Independent Study
cards.subtitle: College library system
cards.notes: Choose Gault when your work needs a more independent-study setting; pair a focused session with a specific reading, outline, or research milestone.
cards.short_summary: Gault is one of Wooster’s three library facilities and is explicitly designated for independent study.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies Gault Library for Independent Study as one of its library system’s three facilities.
cards.access_notes: Library access and service hours vary by term; verify current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Timken Science Library
cards.subtitle: Science-library study space
cards.notes: Use this library for a quiet individual work block, especially when your task calls for sustained reading or writing rather than group conversation.
cards.short_summary: Timken is part of Wooster’s library system and has been described by campus librarians as a silent study space.
cards.evidence_claim: A 2024 Wooster Voice report quotes the College librarian describing Timken Science Library as a silent study space.
cards.source_title: Various departments responded to their respective ratings and answered some students’ comments from The Voice’s approval ratings survey
cards.access_notes: Keep conversation minimal; library hours may be extended during exam periods but should be checked currently.

cards.title: Scot Center
cards.subtitle: Recreation, fitness, and campus events
cards.notes: Build a movement break into a study day by using the fitness equipment or joining an approved activity; confirm facility access requirements first.
cards.short_summary: Scot Center brings fitness equipment and activity spaces together in one campus facility.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says Scot Center offers circuit-training stations, running machines, rowing machines, and free weights.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to College facility policies and event schedules; check current recreation information before arrival.

cards.entity_name: The College of Wooster Art Museum
cards.title: The College of Wooster Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Ebert Art Center, 1220 Beall Ave.
cards.notes: Set aside a short gallery visit between commitments, then use the self-guided sculpture tour to extend the walk across campus at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: The campus museum presents exhibitions, supports learning, and anchors a self-guided sculpture tour.
cards.evidence_claim: The College states that the Art Museum and all of its events are free and open to the public, and offers a self-guided campus sculpture tour.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are posted by the museum; it is on the north side of Ebert Art Center and has an accessible path.

cards.title: McGaw Chapel
cards.subtitle: Campus ceremony and performance setting
cards.notes: Watch the campus calendar for a concert, ceremony, or arts program here, and arrive with enough time to settle in before the program begins.
cards.short_summary: McGaw Chapel is used for student welcome programming and campus arts performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s new-student schedule places the New Students Welcome at McGaw Chapel, while The Wooster Voice documented its use for Celebration of the Arts.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled programs; public-event seating and accessibility details are posted with individual events.

cards.title: Freedlander Theatre
cards.subtitle: Theatre and dance performance venue
cards.notes: Check the theatre-and-dance schedule for a student production or dance concert, then plan your arrival around the ticketing or seating instructions for that show.
cards.short_summary: Freedlander is a long-running campus venue for plays, dance concerts, and opera performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wooster Voice reports that Freedlander Theatre has hosted more than 400 productions, including department plays, dance concerts, and Ohio Light Opera performances.
cards.access_notes: Admission and access depend on the specific performance; verify the current event listing before attending.

cards.title: Kauke Hall Steps
cards.subtitle: Orientation photo and procession site
cards.notes: Pause here when you want a recognizable campus landmark for a group photo, and leave room for any scheduled class or orientation activity using the steps.
cards.short_summary: The Kauke Hall steps serve as a shared setting for new-student class photos and the March Through the Arch.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s new-student orientation schedule lists both the class photo and March Through the Arch at Kauke Hall Steps.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is generally weather-dependent; yield to official ceremonies and scheduled campus programming.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission activities at campus and Wooster destinations with direct, current public-access evidence.

cards.entity_name: The College of Wooster Art Museum
cards.title: Browse the Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Ebert Art Center, 1220 Beall Ave.
cards.notes: Meet at the galleries and take a slow lap through the current exhibitions; check the museum page for its seasonal reopening and regular hours.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission gallery visit with changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The College states that the Art Museum and all of its events are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The museum page lists regular hours and notes a summer closure; confirm it is open before going.

cards.entity_name: College of Wooster Campus Sculpture Tour
cards.title: Walk the Campus Sculpture Tour
cards.subtitle: Self-guided route around The College of Wooster
cards.notes: Download the tour guide, pick a starting point, and walk the route together while stopping at each of the eight documented campus artworks.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided walk connecting eight campus sculptures.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Art Museum offers a self-guided campus sculpture tour featuring eight works of art.
cards.access_notes: Use the downloadable tour guide on the museum page; this is an outdoor self-guided activity.

cards.title: Take a Garden Walk at Secrest
cards.subtitle: Ohio State CFAES Wooster Campus
cards.notes: Set an unhurried walking loop through the gardens and paved paths, then use the seating or picnic sites for a conversation break.
cards.short_summary: A 110-acre botanical garden with free daily admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State describes Secrest Arboretum as a 110-acre botanical garden whose gardens are open daily from dawn to dusk, with free parking and admission.
cards.access_notes: Open to visitors daily from dawn to dusk; parking and admission are free.

cards.title: Explore the Adventure Garden
cards.subtitle: Secrest Arboretum, Ohio State CFAES Wooster Campus
cards.notes: Add the hillside slide and play area to a Secrest walk, then regroup at the surrounding seating or picnic sites before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A named play area inside Secrest Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State identifies the Adventure Garden as a hillside slide and play area at Secrest Arboretum, where parking and admission are free.
cards.access_notes: Use during Secrest's dawn-to-dusk visitor hours; parking and admission are free.

cards.title: Sit in the Garden Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Secrest Arboretum, 2122 Williams Rd.
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a quiet outdoor catch-up in the 200-seat garden amphitheater, then continue along the arboretum’s paved walkways.
cards.short_summary: A 200-seat outdoor amphitheater within the free arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Ohio State lists the 200-seat John Streeter Garden Amphitheater among Secrest Arboretum features and says parking and admission are free.
cards.access_notes: Access it during Secrest's dawn-to-dusk visitor hours; parking and admission are free.

cards.title: Claim a First-Come Pavilion Table
cards.subtitle: Cohan Park, Wooster
cards.notes: Check the pavilion bulletin board, then use an unreserved table for a picnic, board game, or low-key group study session outdoors.
cards.short_summary: A public pavilion available without a reservation when unreserved.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Wooster says park pavilions are always free for public use and otherwise available first-come, first-served; Cohan Pavilion is listed as reservable.
cards.access_notes: Free when not reserved; consult the posted rental schedule and move along if a permit holder arrives.

cards.title: Meet Under Pavilion #1
cards.subtitle: Freedlander Park, 400 Hillside Dr.
cards.notes: Use Pavilion #1 as a no-cost meetup point for conversation or a bring-your-own snack break after walking through the public park.
cards.short_summary: A named public park pavilion with first-come access when unreserved.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Wooster says park pavilions are always free for public use and otherwise available first-come, first-served; Freedlander Pavilion #1 is listed as reservable.
cards.access_notes: Free when not reserved; check the pavilion bulletin board because permitted reservations take priority.

cards.title: Settle In at Jaycee Park Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Jaycee Park, Wooster
cards.notes: Make this an outdoor reading or conversation stop; arrive without a booking and use it only if no reservation is posted for that day.
cards.short_summary: A city pavilion usable free of charge when unreserved.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Wooster says park pavilions are always free for public use and otherwise available first-come, first-served; Jaycee Park Pavilion is listed as reservable.
cards.access_notes: Free when unreserved; a paid reservation guarantees use, so follow any posted permit.

cards.title: Gather at Knights Field Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Knights Field, Wooster
cards.notes: Use the pavilion as a free place to meet before or after a walk; keep plans flexible in case the day has a posted reservation.
cards.short_summary: A named city pavilion with free public use when it is open.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Wooster says park pavilions are always free for public use and otherwise available first-come, first-served; Knights Field Pavilion is listed as reservable.
cards.access_notes: Free when unreserved; check the posted rental schedule and yield the space to permit holders.

cards.title: Plan a Pavilion Conversation Break
cards.subtitle: Schellin Park, Wooster
cards.notes: Bring a book, sketchpad, or friends and use the open pavilion for a relaxed outdoor break, without paying to reserve a time.
cards.short_summary: A public park pavilion with no-charge first-come use.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Wooster says park pavilions are always free for public use and otherwise available first-come, first-served; Schellin Park Pavilion is listed as reservable.
cards.access_notes: Free when unreserved; paid reservations may be posted and take priority.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct study environments documented by The College of Wooster Libraries’ current carrel policy, spanning silent, quiet, and collaborative settings.

cards.title: Andrews Lower 2
cards.subtitle: Andrews Library · silent-study area
cards.notes: Bring a reading-heavy task and settle into the lower second level. The Libraries designate this area for silent study, so keep calls and group work elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A library level designated for silent study.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists Andrews Lower 2 as a silent-study area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; observe the silent-study designation.

cards.title: Andrews/Gault 3
cards.subtitle: Andrews–Gault Library · silent-study area
cards.notes: Use this third-level library area when you need a no-conversation setting. Save collaborative review, meetings, and presentation practice for designated collaboration zones.
cards.short_summary: A third-level silent-study environment in the library complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists Andrews/Gault 3 as a silent-study area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; observe the silent-study designation.

cards.title: Crow's Nest
cards.subtitle: Gault 4 · silent-study area
cards.notes: Head to Gault’s fourth-floor Crow's Nest for an explicitly silent setting. Pack headphones only for personal listening and move any discussion to a collaboration area.
cards.short_summary: The named fourth-floor Gault silent-study area.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy identifies Gault 4, called the Crow's Nest, as a silent-study area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; observe the silent-study designation.

cards.title: Timken Science Library
cards.subtitle: Frick Hall · silent-study area
cards.notes: Choose Timken for science-library resources in a silent-study setting. Keep the workspace quiet and take project conversations or group problem-solving to another location.
cards.short_summary: A science-library setting designated for silent work.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists Timken Science Library as a silent-study area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; observe the silent-study designation.

cards.title: Gault 1
cards.subtitle: Gault Library · quiet-study area
cards.notes: Set up in Gault 1 for work that benefits from a quiet atmosphere without the stricter silent-zone designation. Keep your volume low and avoid extended group discussion.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-study area on Gault’s first level.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists Gault 1 as a quiet-study area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; observe the quiet-study designation.

cards.title: Andrews/Gault 2
cards.subtitle: Andrews–Gault Library · quiet-study area
cards.notes: Use the second level for individual tasks where a quiet setting is helpful. Be considerate of others working nearby and relocate meetings to a collaboration area.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-study environment on the second library level.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists Andrews/Gault 2 as a quiet-study area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; observe the quiet-study designation.

cards.title: Andrews 1
cards.subtitle: Andrews Library · collaboration area
cards.notes: Bring a project partner to Andrews 1 for discussion-based work. This level is designated for collaboration, making it a better fit for conversation than silent floors.
cards.short_summary: A first-level Andrews workspace for collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists Andrews 1 as a collaboration area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; collaboration is designated here.

cards.title: CoRE
cards.subtitle: Andrews Library · collaboration area
cards.notes: Use the Collaborative Research Environment for group planning, project discussion, or shared research tasks. Its library designation supports collaborative rather than silent work.
cards.short_summary: The library’s named collaborative research workspace.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists CoRE as a collaboration area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; collaboration is designated here.

cards.title: Andrews Lower 1
cards.subtitle: Andrews Library · collaboration area
cards.notes: Plan a working session in Andrews Lower 1 when conversation and shared materials are part of the task. Leave it orderly for other library users afterward.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level Andrews area designated for collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Wooster Libraries’ carrel policy lists Andrews Lower 1 as a collaboration area.
cards.access_notes: The policy says the Libraries are public buildings and the public has access to all library areas; collaboration is designated here.

cards.title: Digital Studio
cards.subtitle: Andrews Library · media-production workspace
cards.notes: Reserve time before arriving if you need media-production equipment or a studio space. Use the suite for editing and making project materials, not as a general silent zone.
cards.short_summary: A library suite for digital-media production and editing.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s current-student resources direct students to reserve time in the Digital Studio suite of studio spaces.
cards.source_title: Current Students | The College of Wooster
cards.access_notes: The College’s current-student page says to reserve time in its suite of studio spaces; availability depends on reservation arrangements.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named destinations on downtown Wooster’s Liberty, Market, and Walnut Street corridors, each with a documented feature to look for.

cards.title: Wayne County Public Library mural
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor — 220 W. Liberty St.
cards.notes: Enter through the Liberty Street doors and pause for Brigid of Artfind Tile’s mural of a child reading with a dog.
cards.short_summary: A library entrance mural makes this Liberty Street stop visually specific.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster identifies the Wayne County Public Library at 220 W. Liberty Street and documents the Artfind Tile mural inside its Liberty-facing entrance.
cards.access_notes: Use the Liberty Street-facing entrance; library access and program availability can vary.

cards.title: Before I Die Wall
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor — 144 W. Liberty St.
cards.notes: Bring a thought you can share: this public art wall invites visitors to complete its reflective prompt in chalk.
cards.short_summary: A participatory public-art wall beside Spoon Market & Deli.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster places the Before I Die Wall at 144 W. Liberty Street and says visitors may add their own response.
cards.access_notes: The wall is outdoors beside Spoon Market & Deli; bring chalk only if you intend to participate.

cards.entity_name: Clark Building / Broken Rocks Cafe & Bakery
cards.title: Clark Building’s lecture-site history
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor — 123 E. Liberty St.
cards.notes: Look up at the Clark Building, then use the historic marker context to connect this address with the former Arcadome Hall.
cards.short_summary: A café address with documented links to the former Arcadome Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster states that the Clark Building at 123 E. Liberty Street, now home to Broken Rocks Cafe & Bakery, replaced the Arcadome Hall site after an 1874 fire.
cards.access_notes: View the building from the public sidewalk; café purchases are optional.

cards.title: Courthouse Atlases
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor — 107 W. Liberty St.
cards.notes: Circle the exterior and look for the four Atlas figures used as architectural supports on the historic courthouse.
cards.short_summary: Sculptural Atlas figures are integrated into the courthouse exterior.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster identifies the Wayne County Courthouse at 107 W. Liberty Street and describes its Atlas/Telamones sculptures as architectural columns.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is from public sidewalks; court operations may affect interior access.

cards.title: Downtown Wooster Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — 117 N. Market St.
cards.notes: Use the pavilion as a landmark in the historic square and check Main Street Wooster’s calendar for public performances or events.
cards.short_summary: A public-square pavilion used for performances and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Wooster lists the Downtown Wooster Pavilion at 117 N. Market Street; Main Street Wooster describes the historic-square space as a venue for performances and events.
cards.access_notes: Public pavilion at the downtown square; event setup or reservations may limit use.

cards.title: Local Roots’ co-op marketplace
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — 140 S. Market St.
cards.notes: Browse the market shelves and rotating local offerings, then check the café counter for the day’s available food and drinks.
cards.short_summary: A year-round local co-op market and café in downtown Wooster.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster identifies Local Roots Market & Cafe at 140 S. Market Street as a local co-op and year-round marketplace for local products.
cards.access_notes: Market and café purchases are optional; check the business directly for current offerings.

cards.entity_name: E&H Ace Hardware / Carver Club site
cards.title: Carver Club site
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — 131 S. Market St.
cards.notes: Pause at the storefront and read the tour’s historical context for the former Carver Club at this South Market Street address.
cards.short_summary: A present-day hardware store at a documented historic-club location.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster’s Civil Rights Walking Tour identifies E&H Ace Hardware at 131 S. Market Street as the former Carver Club site.
cards.access_notes: View the historic-site context from the public sidewalk; retail access follows store operations.

cards.entity_name: Blue Spruce Boutique / Brenner Brothers site
cards.title: Brenner Brothers building details
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor — 116 E. Liberty St.
cards.notes: Look for the “Bs” high on the art deco façade and in the entry art while you pass this historic commercial address.
cards.short_summary: An art deco storefront with visible Brenner Brothers references.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster identifies Blue Spruce Boutique at 116 E. Liberty Street as the former Brenner Brothers site and notes visible “Bs” on the building.
cards.access_notes: Exterior architectural details are visible from the public sidewalk; boutique purchases are optional.

cards.entity_name: Children’s Arch at Wayne Center for the Arts
cards.title: Children’s Arch
cards.subtitle: Walnut Street corridor — 237 S. Walnut St.
cards.notes: Walk to Wayne Center for the Arts to see the Children’s Arch, which Main Street Wooster says moved there permanently in 2020.
cards.short_summary: A named public artwork at the Wayne Center for the Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster states that the Children’s Arch was moved in 2020 to its permanent home at Wayne Center for the Arts.
cards.access_notes: View from the arts-center grounds or confirm gallery/building access directly before entering.

cards.title: Historic Downtown Wooster Public Square
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — at Liberty and Market streets
cards.notes: Use the square for a short outdoor pause, then look for the scheduled Main Street Music or other public arts programming.
cards.short_summary: The downtown square is a documented setting for public arts activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street Wooster describes the historic Downtown Wooster Public Square as an open public space used for performances, outdoor dances, and Main Street Music.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space at the Liberty and Market Street intersection; programming is event-dependent.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented College of Wooster traditions, from first-year welcome rites to Independent Study celebrations and longstanding campus symbols.

cards.title: March Through the Arch
cards.subtitle: New Student Orientation at Kauke Hall
cards.notes: Join the scheduled new-student procession from Kauke Hall’s steps through the Arch, then continue to the welcome program.
cards.short_summary: A formal first-day passage through Kauke Hall’s defining Arch.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s 2026 New Student Orientation schedule lists March Through the Arch at 4:30 p.m. at Kauke Hall steps.
cards.source_title: New Students | The College of Wooster
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of New Student Orientation; follow the current orientation schedule.

cards.title: I.S. Monday
cards.subtitle: Independent Study project submission day
cards.notes: If you are a senior finishing Independent Study, check the academic calendar and take part in the submission-day celebration.
cards.short_summary: The signature celebration tied to seniors’ Independent Study submissions.
cards.evidence_claim: Wooster describes the final day for Independent Study project submissions as I.S. Monday, its signature senior-class celebration.
cards.access_notes: For seniors submitting Independent Study; confirm the deadline and event details with the College.

cards.title: The I.S. Tootsie Roll
cards.subtitle: Independent Study hand-in ritual
cards.notes: After submitting an Independent Study project, receive the small candy marker described by the College alongside the completion button.
cards.short_summary: A Tootsie Roll marks the hand-in of a senior research project.
cards.evidence_claim: Wooster states that seniors handing in research projects receive a Tootsie Roll and an “I Did It!” button.
cards.access_notes: Distributed in connection with senior Independent Study project submission.

cards.title: The “I Did It!” Button
cards.subtitle: Independent Study completion keepsake
cards.notes: Look for the black-and-gold completion button when submitting Independent Study, and keep it as a record of the milestone.
cards.short_summary: A black-and-gold button accompanies Independent Study submission.
cards.evidence_claim: Wooster identifies a black-and-gold “I Did It!” button as part of the Independent Study hand-in tradition.
cards.access_notes: Distributed in connection with senior Independent Study project submission.

cards.title: The Culture Show
cards.subtitle: International Education Week at McGaw Chapel
cards.notes: Attend or support the annual student cultural-performance program during International Education Week; consult the current campus calendar for details.
cards.short_summary: A student-led cultural showcase anchored in International Education Week.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies the International Education Week Culture Show as a major collaborative student production.
cards.source_title: Campus Life at Wooster | The College of Wooster
cards.access_notes: Event timing and admission details vary; check the current International Education Week schedule.

cards.title: Scot Spirit Day
cards.subtitle: Annual student-organization fair
cards.notes: Use the annual fair to meet organization leaders and ask directly about joining, upcoming events, and participation requirements.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus fair for connecting with student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wooster Voice describes Scot Spirit Day as the College’s annual student-led organization fair.
cards.source_title: Scot Spirit Day provides opportunities to join over 120 organizations
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current date, location, and participating organizations through Student Activities.

cards.entity_name: Fill the Kauke Arch with Snow
cards.title: Fill the Arch with Snow
cards.subtitle: Kauke Hall winter tradition
cards.notes: Treat this as a documented winter-campus legend, observe any College guidance, and keep all building entrances clear for access and safety.
cards.short_summary: Students have long tried to pack snow to the top of Kauke Hall’s Arch.
cards.evidence_claim: The College notes that Kauke Hall has one Arch available for students to attempt to fill with snow each winter.
cards.source_title: Fast Facts | The College of Wooster
cards.access_notes: Winter conditions and College safety direction apply; do not block other Kauke Hall entrances.

cards.title: Take Your Wooster Brick
cards.subtitle: Graduation keepsake tradition
cards.notes: If graduating, ask the College for current procedures before removing your personal campus brick; do not remove any unapproved material.
cards.short_summary: Graduates have continued a tradition of taking a personal Wooster brick.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s presidential prospectus says generations of alumni have continued the tradition of removing their personal Wooster brick at graduation.
cards.source_title: The College of Wooster Presidential Prospectus
cards.access_notes: Obtain current College authorization and instructions before participating.

cards.title: Wear the MacLeod Tartan
cards.subtitle: Scottish-heritage campus symbol
cards.notes: Spot the MacLeod tartan at Wooster occasions and alumni gatherings; use the College’s current event guidance if choosing attire.
cards.short_summary: MacLeod tartan is a recognized visual marker in Wooster tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Wooster lists MacLeod Tartan among traditions that connect its campus community.
cards.source_title: Discover Wooster | The College of Wooster
cards.access_notes: Appropriate attire guidance varies by event; the College’s Reunion Weekend FAQ says MacLeod tartan is acceptable attire.

cards.title: Follow the Pipe Band to the Field
cards.subtitle: Fighting Scots football gameday entrance
cards.notes: At a home football game, watch the Pipe Band lead the Fighting Scots onto the field and follow venue instructions for spectators.
cards.short_summary: Bagpipes frame the Fighting Scots’ gameday entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: The College states that its Pipe Band leads the Fighting Scots football team onto the field on gamedays.
cards.source_title: The College of Wooster Presidential Prospectus
cards.access_notes: Occurs at home football games; verify the current athletics schedule and spectator information.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at The College of Wooster, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that starts with campus bearings, adds food and arts, and leaves room for recreation or a scheduled event.

cards.title: Start with a self-guided campus loop
cards.subtitle: First stop · 847 College Avenue
cards.notes: Pick up a campus map by the Admissions Office entrance, then use the self-guided walk to place the buildings you will revisit.
cards.short_summary: Begin by turning the campus map into a familiar route.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says campus maps are available next to the Gault Admissions Center entrance and welcomes self-guided tours.
cards.access_notes: Use the self-guided-tour option; office services may follow separate hours.

cards.title: Find the steps and arch at Kauke Hall
cards.subtitle: Orientation landmark · campus center
cards.notes: Walk to the steps while you are orienting yourself; this is the documented gathering point for the new-student class photo and March Through the Arch.
cards.short_summary: Locate a recognizable orientation landmark early.
cards.evidence_claim: The College's 2026 new-student orientation schedule lists the class photo and March Through the Arch at Kauke Hall Steps.
cards.source_title: New Students | The College of Wooster
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; no event access is implied outside its scheduled use.

cards.title: Make Lowry your meal-and-meetup anchor
cards.subtitle: Midday stop · Dining Hall and Allen Commons
cards.notes: Use a meal break to learn the building: the Dining Hall and Allen Commons both appear in the College’s new-student orientation schedule.
